built_from: ../../sources/limits-of-observability.data.json (the hub rows the asks link to)

L08.statement: The 6-column shire grid spans about 22.2 mm, 86% of the die width; the rest is the memory shires and their LPDDR4x PHYs down each side.
L08.note: Tile outlines at x ≈ 139.5–1649.5 px. The heat-per-mm drawing places tiles at the 3.73 mm period, so its grid looks slightly wider than 86% (its caption says so).

L09.statement: Each side strip (memory shires + LPDDR4x PHYs) is about 1.76 mm wide (1.74 and 1.80 mm for the two strips).

L101.statement: The mesh (routers, links, NetSpeed bridges) is on its own low-voltage rail at 0.485 V (0.484 V at the die).

L102.statement: Every shire's NoC port is 512 bits wide: one 64 B line per beat, single-beat only.

L103.statement: A shire has 4 to_l3 master and 4 L3 slave lanes to the mesh; the lane is chosen by PA[7:6], so lines i and i+4 share a lane (a 1 KB load puts 4 of its 16 lines on each).

L104.statement: The mesh routes in dimension order, and a request and its reply take opposite orders: a request goes x first, then y, and a reply y first, then x, on the logical map, so a reply retraces its request's route backwards. Measured on 29 September (E56) with sets of streams between shires chosen so that their streams share one directed link under one order and none under the other: 1 KB tensor loads, whose data travel as replies, fell to 0.54-0.77 of their bandwidth alone when they shared a link under y first and held at 1.00 when they shared one under x first; tensor stores, whose data travel as requests, showed the mirror (0.52-0.76 against 1.00). A shared link carried about 92 GB/s. The same on aifoundry1 card 1 (development), aifoundry3 (the frozen validation) and aifoundry2 (the same frozen test, run as a third card on the evening of 29 September), three passes each.
L104.source: tools/claims-v3/nocr/PREREG.md (frozen 29 Sep about 00:10 PDT, sha256 2472ab3e...; the sets: workloads/nocroute/meshmap.py, tools/claims-v3/nocr/sets.json); docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr/raw/<card>/summary.json .r32.read and .r32.write: .verdict, .sets.<set>.rho_pooled (sets of 3 and 5 streams), .capacity_gbs_from_dropping_sets; docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr/README.md
L104.note: Until 29 September this fact was inferred: the analyses assumed x first for every packet (as Chang infers), and every route on this page was drawn so (docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b 'Routing'; heat-per-mm.script.js's route map, x first by default until 29 September: its `order` and the 'Routing order' toggle). What E56 saw is the data: a load's replies and a store's requests. That a load's own requests go x first and a store's acknowledgements y first follows if the order is set by the kind of packet; those small packets never slowed a set (each costs a link under 0.54 of a reply). On the die view x runs down the die's rows: a request first moves north or south, then east or west, and a reply first east or west.

L105.statement: Each mesh stop has 9 main-NoC routers (layers 0–8) plus one debug-NoC router; routers have 8 ports (H, E, S, W, N, I, J, K) with 4 VC slots each; route info, packet, sideband and data are parity-protected (no ECC).
L105.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b rows 'Main-NoC layers', 'Router ports and VCs', 'Error protection' (etsoc_shire_other_esr.h:3877-3981; noc_esr.h)
L105.note: SYNTHESIS marks these 'U' (not independently re-verified); router-to-router flit width is unknown.

L11.statement: A minion-shire cell is about 13.8–13.95 mm²; the 34 minion shires take about 468–474 mm² (82–83% of the die).

L111.statement: The shire cache is 4 MB in 4 banks × 4 sub-banks (the POR for the first SoC); 64 B lines everywhere.

L114.statement: Shire top level: the main NoC interface (ports to_l3 ×4, to_sys, l3_slave ×4, uc_to_l3, uc_to_sys, sys_slave) sits above the shire channel (shire cache with 4 banks, UC block, RBOX, ESR, I$ memories), which feeds the four neighbourhoods; clock domains CLOCK_NOC, SHIRE_CLOCK, NEIGH_CLOCK, with the PLL/DLL, sensors and debug NoC bridge below.
L114.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf p.5 Figure 1
L114.note: A logical block diagram, not a floorplan: no source gives where the four neighbourhoods and four banks sit physically inside the 3.7 mm tile.

L115.statement: Neighbourhood floorplan: two columns of four minions either side of a central 'neighbourhood channel'; left column M2, M0, M4, M6 and right column M3, M1, M5, M7 (north to south); all ports and the high-voltage region are at the north end, where it meets the shire channel.
L115.note: Placed to shorten the fast local messaging network: its tree edges 0–1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7 cross the channel and 0–2, 0–4, 4–6 are vertical neighbours (L116).

L116.statement: Inside a shire only the reduction-tree edges are fast: 68 cycles (113 ns) round trip for 28 pairs per shire (in every neighbourhood 0–1, 0–2, 0–4, 2–3, 4–5, 4–6, 6–7) and 114–115 cycles (190 ns) for all 468 others, in every pass on three cards.

L121.statement: 35 sensors are read: TS0–TS31 for the compute shires (TSn in shire n), TS32 master, TS33 spare, TS34 I/O; the PCIe shire has no sensor.

L123.statement: Per-shire on-die voltage at idle (34 minion shires): minion rail 517–521 mV, lows 513 (shires 0, 1, 2, 18) to 520, highs to 522; SRAM 703–707 mV; mesh 483–486 mV.

L23.statement: The datasheet block diagram (Figure 2-6) also puts the PCIe shire then the I/O shire at the east end of the top row, the memory shires on the west and east edges, and the LPDDR4X interfaces outside them: two LPDDR4X blocks per side, each beside two memory shires.
L23.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.15 Figure 2-6 'ET-SoC-1 Block Diagram'
L23.note: Read from the figure; the diagram is schematic (it draws the shire array 4 wide). Consistent with DS p.30: 'Two Memshires communicate with each 64-bit LPDDR4X memory device'.

L24.statement: Top-row order conflicts between sources: PRM Fig. 1-3 has PCIe in the fifth column and I/O in the sixth; the die plot with its MPR caption has I/O (purple, Maxion) fifth and PCIe (orange) sixth. The two are mirror images.
L24.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1a row 'Top-row order'; docs/reports/sources/heat-per-mm.script.js:102 ('the two sources disagree on the order')
L24.note: Unresolved; the heat-per-mm die drawing labels both cells 'PCIe or I/O'.

L25.statement: ESR shire IDs: 0–33 are minion shires 0–33, 232–239 are memory shires 0–7, 253 is the PCIe shire, 254 the I/O shire, 255 means 'the local minion shire'.
L25.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.487 §15 (ESR address bits 29:22 encode the shire ID)

L26.statement: The master shire is shire 32 and the spare shire is shire 33 (the last of NUM_SHIRES = 34).

L28.statement: The PCIe shire holds two independent PCI Express controllers and an 8-lane PCIe physical interface (Gen4, up to 25.78 Gb/s per lane).
L28.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.8 §1.2; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.4 §1

L29.statement: The I/O shire holds a Maxion neighbourhood of four ET-Maxion cores, another 4 MB L2/L3, the service processor with its ROM and 1 MB scratchpad SRAM, a hardware root of trust, USB, I2C, SPI and UARTs; the five PVT controllers also sit in it.
L29.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.8 §1.2 and p.17 §1.6

L31.statement: The four grey cells of the logical map are (0,3), (0,4), (0,5) and (5,3). They hold the master shire, the spare shire, the PCIe shire and the I/O shire, which route traffic too; which is which was not measured.
L31.note: analyze.py:50-51: marty1885's bandwidth data shows (5,3) routes traffic.

L32.statement: Inferred identities: (0,4) and (0,5) are the I/O and PCIe shires, in some order (the two top-row cells beside each other on the die); (0,3) and (5,3) are the master and spare shires, in some order.
L32.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1a row 'Logical map vs die'; docs/reports/2026-09-22-et-soc1-spatial-temperature-brief.html:765-786 (cells labelled 'master or spare' and 'I/O or PCIe', 'inferred'); superseded 27 Sep by fw.grey-cells
L32.note: Superseded 27 Sep: the firmware's maps name the four cells (fact fw.grey-cells): (0,3) the master (shire 32), (5,3) the spare (33), (0,4) the PCIe shire and (0,5) the I/O shire, the order of PRM Fig. 1-3. Timing a counter read on shire 32 confirms the master's cell on a card: E56 (29 Sep, docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr) placed it there on aifoundry1 card 1 and decided nothing on aifoundry3 or aifoundry2.

L33.statement: The logical map appears to be the die turned a quarter: in map orientation the memory shires sit above and below the grid; on the die (and in the firmware's naming, 0–3 west, 4–7 east) they are the two side columns. Logical x runs north–south (die rows) and y runs east–west (die columns).
L33.source: docs/reports/2026-09-18-et-soc1-on-chip-communication.html:719; docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html:780-783; docs/et-soc1-notes.md:104-105; docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1a row 'Logical map vs die'; settled 27 Sep by fw.map-match except the handedness (die.handedness)
L33.note: Settled 27 Sep except the east-west handedness: the firmware's NoC-spec map, renamed as the boot firmware renames the shires, equals the measured map in every pair distance with no rotation or mirror (fact fw.map-match); which handedness the silicon has is open (fact die.handedness). Distances alone cannot tell a rotation from a reflection.

L34.statement: Die-orientation 8 × 6 view (north row first, west column first; MS = memory shire, None = empty corner): None 0 8 3 grey grey grey None | MS0 24 16 4 12 20 28 MS4 | MS1 9 1 13 21 29 5 MS5 | MS2 25 17 14 22 30 6 MS6 | MS3 2 10 18 26 15 7 MS7 | None 11 19 27 grey 23 31 None.
L34.source: derived from workloads/nocbench/analyze.py:52-60 (MARTY) with the mapping of docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1a ('Logical x runs N–S and y runs E–W'; '(0,3) = top row col 4, (0,4)/(0,5) = I/O and PCIe, (5,3) = bottom row col 4') and the memory-shire fit of docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html:864; settled 27 Sep by fw.map-match except the handedness (die.handedness)
L34.note: Settled 27 Sep except the east-west handedness: this view is the firmware's NoC-spec map after the boot-time renaming (fact fw.map-match), and the firmware names the grey cells (fw.grey-cells). Memory shire 2's row is still a tie-break of the fit (L42, ms2-forced).

L37.statement: A firmware comment gives a 'default Shire Virtual ID Map, based on the NOC spec' in die orientation: rows 0 16 12 4 253 254 | 1 8 24 28 20 5 | 9 17 25 29 21 13 | 2 18 26 30 22 6 | 10 3 27 31 7 14 | 11 19 32 33 23 15, with mc0–mc3 on the west and mc4–mc7 on the east. As written it does not match the measured map: only 111 of 496 shire pairs have the same Manhattan distance, and 15 of the 51 measured one-hop pairs are adjacent in it.
L37.source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/include/noc_reconfigure.h:76-82 (comparison computed here against workloads/nocbench/analyze.py MARTY); superseded 27 Sep by fw.map-match (the map after the boot firmware renames the shires)
L37.note: Superseded: this compares the map before NOC_Remap_Shires renames the shires at boot; after the renaming it matches all 496 pair distances (fact fw.map-match).

L40.statement: Fitting DRAM latency with one shared constant plus 12 cycles per hop, and each memory shire one hop outside the grid, puts memory shires 0–3 above the grid and 4–7 below it at x = 1…4 (logical frame): MS0 (1,-1), MS1 (2,-1), MS2 (3,-1), MS3 (4,-1), MS4 (1,6), MS5 (2,6), MS6 (3,6), MS7 (4,6); total squared error 2 cycles² over 32 home/memory-shire pairs.
L40.note: The fit tried only positions one hop outside the grid; moving all eight one hop further out fits equally with a constant of 79.

L41.statement: The memory-shire leg is 91 cycles plus 12 per hop between the L3 home shire and the memory shire (fitted constant); refitted pass by pass on three cards the constant reads 90–91.

L42.statement: Memory shire 2's position is a tie-break: its four home shires all sit in column x = 4, so x = 3 or x = 5 above the grid, or (6, 0) beside it, fit equally.

L43.statement: The memory shire that serves a line is picked by physical-address bits 8:6 and its L3 home shire by bits 10:6, so memory shire m serves the lines of home shires m, m+8, m+16 and m+24. Hardware read counters confirmed the memory-shire bits for 64 of 64 lines (and in all 15 passes of the three-card check).
L43.note: 'm, m+8, m+16, m+24' is derived from the two bit fields (bits 8:6 are the low three bits of 10:6).

L44.statement: With the memory shires one hop outside the grid, the memory shire's position adds 12–84 cycles to a DRAM load (1–7 hops from the L3 home).
L44.note: Recomputed from MARTY and ms_pos: home→memory-shire distance is 1–7 hops, mean 2.625.

L45.statement: Whole DRAM load: latency = 110 + 12·hops(requester → L3 home) + 91 + 12·hops(L3 home → memory shire). Left as fitted, the model is within ±3 cycles for 97% of loads on aifoundry2, 93% on aifoundry3 and 94% on aifoundry1's card 1.

L46.statement: Of the 91-cycle memory-shire constant (152 ns), the DRAM chip accounts for about 25–28 cycles (activate tRCD 11 cycles = 18 ns, 19.3 ns read latency, one or two 4.3 ns bursts); at most ~63–66 cycles (~105–110 ns) are the memory shire itself: controller queue, PHY and the crossings between the 933 MHz DDR clock and the mesh.
L46.note: 'At most' because each hop further out moves 12 cycles from the constant into the mesh legs.

L47.statement: Each memory shire drives two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels (16 in all, four external LPDDR4X chips of four 16-bit channels = 64 bits each); two memory shires share each 64-bit LPDDR4X device, at up to 4,266 Mb/s per pin.
L47.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.17 §1.5; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.30 §7 and §7.1
L47.note: The manuals differ on controllers: PRM p.17 'two memory controllers that each have a 16-bit LPDDR4X channel'; DS p.30 'two 16-bit LPDDR4X physical interfaces sharing a single 32-bit controller'. docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:286 follows the PRM (2 uMCTL2 per memshire).

L48.statement: Each memory shire has a 512-bit NoC memory port; the datasheet gives the NoC side a maximum of 32 GB/s per memory shire, almost twice the sustained LPDDR4X throughput behind it.
L48.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.30 §7.1.1 and §7.1.1.1

L50.statement: DRAM address map: PA[9] selects the controller (channel) within the memory shire, PA[12:10] the DRAM bank (8 banks), PA[34:18] the row; the page policy is open-page. Measured on 29 September (E57): another row in the same bank is a row conflict, and a row that also differs in any of PA[6-12] (the memory shire, the controller, the bank) reads as a row hit, 20 cycles faster, on aifoundry1-c1 and aifoundry3 (15 of 15 conditions); on aifoundry3 and aifoundry2 PA[6-9] set the refresh phase and PA[10-13] and PA[18] do not, so each controller refreshes on its own. On aifoundry2, run the same way as a third card, 14 of 15 conditions came out so: two lines that differ only in PA[17], a column bit in this map, read as a row conflict there.
L50.source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:66-85; measured: tools/claims-v3/memp2/prereg/PREREG.md (lock 9712c3d6...), docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-memp2/val-aifoundry3/memp2.json, val-aifoundry2/memp2.json and dev-aifoundry1-c1/memp2.json .cards.<card>.items.R33a.per_cond, .misclassified, .R33b.refresh_domain_bits, .R33c
L50.note: Inferred until 29 September (from a tool comment, NoC mask values and ADDRMAP registers, not a readback). E57 measured the bank and row split on aifoundry1-c1 and aifoundry3 (R33a; on aifoundry2 14 of 15 conditions, PA[17] reading as a row bit there) and the refresh domain on aifoundry3 and aifoundry2 (R33b; on aifoundry1-c1 PA[7] read unclear and no registered reading fitted). Still open: whether two accesses on one controller serialise (R33c, insufficient on all three cards), and why PA[17] conflicts on aifoundry2.

L70.statement: TensorSend 32 B round trip between shires = 150 + 12.02 × (Manhattan hops) cycles at 600 MHz, worst residual 1.1–1.4 cycles over all 496 pairs, on each of three cards.
L70.note: Per card: aifoundry2 149.99 + 12.017 (worst 1.40); aifoundry3 150.01 + 12.015 (worst 1.08); aifoundry1-c1 150.06 + 12.017 (worst 1.10). First session (aifoundry2, 18 Sep): 149.97 + 12.021, worst 1.13.

L71.statement: Intercept of the between-shire round trip: 150 cycles (the fixed cost of leaving and re-entering shires).

L72.statement: Each mesh hop adds 20 ns round trip: 12 minion cycles at 600 MHz, 16 at 800; a hop is 20 ns at either clock. In time, 250 ns + 20 ns per hop across shires, r² 0.9999 over 496 pairs.

L79.statement: Where the requester sits matters: L3 (4 MB working set) 168.8–168.9 cycles from shires 0 and 31, 160.6–160.7 from 7, 159.1–159.2 from 24; DRAM (256 MB) 296.6–297.1 from 0 and 31, 287.2–288.8 from 7 and 24. L3(0) − L3(24) = 9.69–9.73 cycles on the three cards.

L80.statement: Why: the mean distance to the 32 L3 slices is 5.000 hops from shire 0, 4.3125 from 7, 4.1875 from 24 and 5.000 from 31 (0 and 31 sit in opposite corners of the map); the difference 0 − 24 is 0.8125 hops × 12 = 9.75 cycles, matching the measured 9.7.
L80.source: computed here from workloads/nocbench/analyze.py MARTY (hops) and the 12 cycles/hop of docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html:837

L86.statement: Ring energy slope per mean hop by card: aifoundry2 1.78 [1.31–2.25], aifoundry3 1.73 [0.48–2.97], aifoundry1 card 1 1.74 [0.95–2.53] pJ/B (99% intervals, 6 passes each); no pair of cards differs; pooled 1.75 (the page gives ±50%).

L87.statement: Inside a shire, messaging costs 0.7–2.2 pJ per byte with 1 KB messages, busy cores included; a byte costs 6–26× more once it crosses the shire boundary.

L91.statement: The shire boundary is a bandwidth cliff: with every minion sending 1 KB messages the chip moves 1.1–3.0 TB/s inside shires but 0.09–0.16 TB/s between them (7–34× less); a TensorLoad from a remote scratchpad does 0.96 TB/s at 600 MHz.

L93.statement: Handing a result to the next shire instead of through DRAM: aifoundry2 111.3 vs 8.61 pJ/B, aifoundry3 107.5 vs 8.27, aifoundry1 card 1 129.9 vs 9.89; DRAM ÷ next shire 12.9–13.1× on every card; own scratchpad 4.05–4.86 pJ/B.
L93.page: Hand it to the next shire: on-chip relay vs DRAM

L94.statement: In the relay, which shire receives the slab moves bandwidth by up to a quarter: 593 GB/s to the next shire by ID (3.5 hops on average, longest hand-off 10) to 733 GB/s at 16 shire IDs (2.1, longest 6); bandwidth falls with the longest hand-off (r = −0.99), about 3,200–3,300 cycles of stage time per hop of it.
L94.note: A correlation over five offsets, not a controlled test (the claims row says so).
L94.page: Hand it to the next shire: on-chip relay vs DRAM

addr.dram-region.statement: The DRAM region starts at 0x80_0000_0000; minions reach only the 'Low' view (M-mode low 8 MB, OS low to 0x80_FFFF_FFFF, memory low 0x81_0000_0000-0x87_FFFF_FFFF, 28 GB); device allocations come back as 0x80_xxxx_xxxx addresses.
addr.dram-region.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.551 (Table 15-96) and p.553 (Table 15-98); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:348-350, 379-380

addr.load-model.statement: Measured load-to-use model from any requesting shire at 600 MHz: L1 5; L2 47-48; L3 110 + 12·hops(requester, home = PA[10:6]); DRAM 110 + 12·hops(requester, home) + 91 + 12·hops(home, memory shire = PA[8:6]). The mesh round trip is paid twice on a DRAM load: to the L3 home, then on to the memory shire.
addr.load-model.source: docs/et-soc1-notes.md:164-166; anatomy page §1 'Trace one load' and headline tiles; docs/findings/05-claims.md:403-404 (V3 check: L3 within ±4 cycles for 99.4-99.97% of lines, DRAM within ±3 for 93-97%)
addr.load-model.note: The model counts hops, not routes. The route order inside the mesh was measured on 29 September (fact L104): each request x first, each reply y first.

addr.load-path.statement: Path of a cacheable load: an L1 miss sends Read_L2 over ET-Link to the local bank chosen by PA[7:6]; an L2 miss sends Read_L3 over the to_l3 mesh interface to the home shire's L3 slave chosen by PA[10:6] (data returns straight to the neighbourhood, before the fill); an L3 miss goes over to_sys to the memory shire chosen by PA[8:6], whose controller does activate/read/precharge.
addr.load-path.note: A synthesis of the Shire Cache Specification and the RTL by the repo's research notes; the measured latency model (next fact) agrees.

addr.regions.statement: 40-bit physical address space (1 TB): I/O 0x00_0000_0000 (1 GB), service processor 0x00_4000_0000 (1 GB), scratchpad 0x00_8000_0000 (2 GB), ESRs 0x01_0000_0000 (4 GB), PCIe 0x40_0000_0000 (256 GB), DRAM 0x80_0000_0000 (512 GB).
addr.regions.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.340 (Table 15-1); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.20 (§3)

ar.tree.statement: The allreduce benchmark's tree: at level h, a minion whose ID has bit h as its lowest set bit sends its partial sum to the minion with that bit cleared (TensorReduce), levels 0 to 9, and the result comes back down the same tree (TensorBroadcast). Levels 0-2 join a neighbourhood's 8 minions along the fast network's edges, levels 3-4 its 4 neighbourhoods, levels 5-9 the 32 shires, rooted at minion 0 of shire 0.
ar.tree.source: workloads/nocbench/kernel/nocbench.c:279-288 (tree: TensorReduce for levels 0..top, TensorBroadcast back), :516-521 ('Minion m receives at levels below ctz(m) and sends at ctz(m); the root (m = 0) receives at every level'); fact neigh.fln-edges for the tree edges

bc.allreduce-1kb.statement: The same hardware allreduce with 1 KB (32 vector registers) instead of 32 B: 1,354 cycles over a shire's 32 minions (1,354.05-1,354.16 in every pass on the three cards, 2.26 µs) and 3,236-3,244 cycles over all 1,024 minions (each card's median over three passes: aifoundry2 3,236.33, aifoundry3 3,243.35, aifoundry1-c1 3,244.27; 5.4 µs at 600 MHz), against 444 and 1,393 cycles for 32 B.
bc.allreduce-1kb.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/raw/<card>/lat/p*/noc/allreduce-c32.jsonl and xallreduce-c32.jsonl (E36; count 32; cycles_per_iter of the one-tree rows at 32 and 1,024 minions), read in build_facts.py; the on-chip communication page's chart shows the same medians (its embedded nocbench-data .v3.cards.<card>.allreduce["32"], analyze.py merge_passes)
bc.allreduce-1kb.note: The claims ledger lists the 32 B allreduces of the same passes (05-claims.md, "Barriers and allreduces"); the 1 KB rows are in the same raw files.

bc.esr-ipi.statement: ESR broadcast: one request writes the same system register in every shire of a mask (32 bits for the compute shires, 8 for the memory shires): software writes the value to the broadcast data register, then the target register and the masks to a broadcast request register. A shire's IPI_TRIGGER register takes a 64-bit mask of its harts and interrupts each hart whose bit is set; the firmware's broadcast system call writes the first two.
bc.esr-ipi.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.511 (§15.4.2 ESR Broadcast, Table 15-85, Figure 15-1, Table 15-86) and p.336 (§13.1 IPI_TRIGGER, Table 13-1); external/et-platform/device-minion-runtime/src/MachineMinion/src/trap_handler.S:83-97 (SYSCALL_BROADCAST_INT writes ESR_SHIRE_BROADCAST0, then BROADCAST1 with the shire mask)

bc.half.statement: The broadcast half of the tree was never timed on its own: nocbench times TensorReduce up the tree and TensorBroadcast back down as one operation, one cycle count around both, so the broadcast is part of the allreduce's 444 cycles over 32 minions and 1,393 over 1,024 (32 B). Neither half's energy was measured: the energy manual's synchronisation table gives none for the tree.
bc.half.source: workloads/nocbench/kernel/nocbench.c:279-288 (tree(): TensorReduce for levels 0..top, then TensorBroadcast top..0) and :529-534 (one cycle count around the repeated tree); docs/energy-manual/06-synchronisation.md:12 (TensorReduce + broadcast: energy '—')

bc.launch-31.statement: Queued back to back, an empty kernel costs the card 103.6 / 103.7 / 104.1 µs on all 32 shires and 91.2 / 92.2 / 92.4 µs on one (aifoundry2 / aifoundry3 / aifoundry1-c1): the other 31 shires add 12.4 / 11.4 / 11.6 µs (11.4-12.4 µs), the rest the same for one shire or 32. Which part of that is the launch's multicast (the interrupt, every hart reading the message, the shires' acknowledging atomics) and which the kernel's own start and finish was not measured.
bc.launch-31.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-pcie/pcie.json launch.<card>.b2b_us."32".mean and ."1".mean (E50), the difference computed in build_facts.py; the Over the PCIe link page's launch note (docs/reports/sources/pcie-link.script.js:241-243)

bc.launch-multicast.statement: Every kernel launch is a broadcast. The master shire's firmware copies the 64-byte launch message into a buffer in its own scratchpad and evicts it to the L2, raises the interrupt on all 64 harts of every shire in the kernel's mask with one ESR broadcast, and polls a shire mask beside the buffer: each hart evicts its stale L1 copy and reads the message, and the last of a shire's 64 harts clears that shire's bit with a global atomic AND. The launch goes on once every bit is clear.
bc.launch-multicast.source: external/et-platform/device-minion-runtime/src/MasterMinion/src/services/cm_iface.c:75-83 (broadcast_ipi_trigger), :270-367 (CM_Iface_Multicast_Send: ETSOC_MEM_COPY_AND_EVICT to the L2 at :318, the interrupt at :322, the poll on the shire mask to :336); src/MasterMinion/src/workers/kw.c:931-933 (the launch: 'Blocking call that blocks till all shires ack command'); src/WorkerMinion/src/mm_to_cm_iface.c:60-73 (notify_mm: the 64th hart clears its shire's bit with atomic_and_global_64), :122-128 (ETSOC_MEM_EVICT before the read); et-common-libs/include/system/layout.h:51, 112-118 (a 64-byte buffer and its control line in the master shire's scratchpad); et-platform 836a4ab

bc.one-request.statement: Inside a shire, requests to one line are kept in order, and 'Two requests to the mesh will never have the same address outstanding': when every minion of a shire loads one line homed in another shire, the shire has at most one request for it on the mesh at a time. The L2's 8-entry read buffer is there for 'multiple readers of the same cache line', its hits 'serviced once per clock'; L3 reads at the home do not use it.
bc.one-request.unit: mesh request per line and shire at a time
bc.one-request.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.36 (§2.6.1 Reqq Request Ordering, rule 1a), p.9 (the Read buffer) and p.40 (§2.8: 'L3 reads do not use the Read buffer')
bc.one-request.note: That the shire's other minions then find the line in its L2 follows from the fill; loads of one line by every minion at once were not measured.

bc.pollers.statement: 31 minions, one in each other shire, hammering one global atomic homed in shire 0 kept its bank retiring one every 10.00 cycles, while shire 0's one minion reading its own scratchpad kept 100% of its rate alone, in three passes on each of the three cards (the prediction was 1% or less). Whether they would stop a shire whose 32 minions all read was not tested. Each shire's leader polling one counter hung the relay's first barrier (one development run).
bc.pollers.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-hotline-aifoundry2/hotline.json: pollers[card=<card>, home="scplocal:0"].remote_cycles_per_atomic (9.9993), .frac_of_alone_n (0.99998-0.99999); docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/lat.json [item=LAT-H].per_card.<card>.sub.P5_pollers (host_over_alone1 1.0 in every pass); docs/findings/17-hot-line.md:137-145; docs/findings/18-on-chip-relay.md:149-152
bc.pollers.page: One hot line stops a shire

bc.tensorbroadcast.statement: TensorBroadcast sends COUNT vector registers of 32 bytes down a fully balanced binary tree: at node height HEIGHT a hart whose mhartid is a multiple of 2^(HEIGHT+2) sends to hart mhartid + 2^(HEIGHT+1), and with FUNCT = MOVE every hart ends with the root's value. N harts take log2 N steps, HEIGHT from log2(N) - 1 down to 0, and each step waits for both of its harts, their vector registers stalled until the data has moved. Hart 0 of minion m is hart 2m, so a broadcast from minion 0 to all 1,024 minions takes ten steps, the first to minion 512, minion 0 of shire 16.
bc.tensorbroadcast.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.320-322 (§9.4, TensorBroadcast: 'performed in a fully-balanced binary-tree fashion', the sender and receiver rule, 'a sequence of log2N TensorBroadcast operations', 'effectively implementing a broadcast of A0', the stall notes); workloads/nocbench/kernel/nocbench.c:279-288 (the benchmark's tree: TensorBroadcast with MOVE from the top level down); workloads/nocbench/README.md (the target is a minion ID, shire * 32 + minion, and the partner is hart 2 * ID)

board.card.statement: The PCIe dev card V3: ET-SoC-1 soldered down, 4 LPDDR4x devices (256-bit), 64 GB eMMC, USB (device/debug, OTG, FTDI UART), JTAG, 12 V input metered by an LTC4218 hot-swap controller.
board.card.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.3 (Features) and pdf p.6-7 (Power Measurement)

board.meters.statement: The PMIC meters the 12 V input and three regulators (minion, NoC, SRAM); DDR, VDDQ, VDDQLP, PCIe logic, PCIe and Maxion rails have set points only. The service processor forwards a new value about every 133 ms (aifoundry2; 224 ms quiet pass on aifoundry3).

bw-dram.statement: DRAM streaming: 76 GB/s for the whole chip (0.124 B per minion-cycle), about 64% of the 119 GB/s that 16 x 16-bit channels carry at 3,733 MT/s; about a twentieth of an A100.
bw-dram.source: ridge-data: levels[dram].measured (bpc 0.1235, gbps 75.9), .spec (gbps 119.5; datasheet max 136.5); docs/findings/05-claims.md:370
bw-dram.note: Tensor stores to DRAM also 76 GB/s on all three cards; stores through the L1 only 27 GB/s (ridge-data limits.write_gbps). The runtime's 128,000 MB/s is a firmware placeholder constant.

bw-l1.statement: L1 hits, 32 B vector loads by both harts: 14.5 TB/s chip-wide (23.6 B per minion-cycle) in the energy manual's unrolled loop; the memory-hierarchy probe's loop reaches 6.2 TB/s (10 B per minion-cycle). Spec: 32 B per cycle.
bw-l1.source: docs/reports/2026-09-18-et-soc1-ridge-points.html ridge-data: levels[l1d].demonstrated (bpc 23.57, gbps 14,480; by card 14,474-14,488), .measured (bpc 10.04, gbps_600 6,211), .spec.bpc 32
bw-l1.note: The 6.2 TB/s figure is aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 (rerun passes); the 14.5 TB/s catalogue figure is on all three cards.
bw-l1.cards_txt: three cards (14.5 TB/s); 6.2 TB/s on aifoundry2, aifoundry3

bw-l2.statement: L2 cache, 1 KB tensor loads by every minion: 2.45 TB/s chip-wide, 4.0 B per minion-cycle (128 B per shire-cycle), half the four banks' 256 B per shire-cycle spec.
bw-l2.note: A lone minion reads 6.4 B per cycle from L2 or scratchpad on all three cards (ridge points, three-card check).

bw-l3.statement: L3, every minion streaming: 0.98 TB/s chip-wide, 1.6 B per minion-cycle; spec (assumed one 64 B beat per NoC cycle per shire port) 3.3 TB/s, 5.33 B per minion-cycle.

bw-pcie.statement: Host link: PCIe Gen4 x8, 15.75 GB/s per direction before protocol overhead; the transfers were timed on three cards on 27 September (facts pcie.h2d and pcie.d2h give the measured rates).
bw-pcie.source: ridge-data: levels[pcie].spec (ET Preliminary Datasheet sec. 1); docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-pcie/pcie.json (27 Sep)
bw-pcie.note: The link figure, not a measurement: measured on 27 September (facts pcie.h2d, pcie.d2h). The ridge row of 05-claims.md that called it never measured predates that.

bw-scp-own.statement: Own-shire scratchpad: 2.46 TB/s chip-wide, 4.0 B per minion-cycle, same as the L2. Tensor stores into it reach 1.23 TB/s (half the read rate).
bw-scp-own.source: ridge-data: levels[scp].measured (bpc 4.000, gbps 2,456); limits.write_gbps.tstore_scp (1,230 on each card)
bw-scp-own.note: Read rate on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3 (rerun passes); the store rate on all three cards.
bw-scp-own.cards_txt: aifoundry2, aifoundry3 (the read rate); the store rate on three cards

bw-scp-remote.statement: Another shire's scratchpad (each shire reading the one 16 IDs away, 2.1 hops on average): 0.96 TB/s chip-wide, 1.56 B per minion-cycle.
bw-scp-remote.note: If many shires read one shire's scratchpad its four mesh ports would allow only about 0.1 TB/s (ridge points, inferred).

bw-tsend-fln.statement: TensorSend on the neighbourhood fast local network (pairs on tree edges), every minion sending 1 KB messages: 2,992 GB/s chip-wide, 4.9 B per minion-cycle.
bw-tsend-fln.note: Rates are one session on aifoundry2 (18 Sep); the energies below are three cards.

bw-tsend-link.statement: One TensorSend link, 1 KB messages: 5.3 GB/s on the fast local network, 2.9 through the shire crossbar, 2.7 over one mesh hop, 1.8 over 10 hops (the three cards agree to the digits).

bw-tsend-mesh.statement: TensorSend between shires: 87-156 GB/s chip-wide over six shire-to-shire ring patterns (0.25 B per minion-cycle at best): 7-34x less message bandwidth than inside a shire.
bw-tsend-mesh.note: Limited by how many packets a sender keeps in flight (3-5 GB/s per shire).

chip-minions.statement: Kernels run on 1,024 minions (32 compute shires x 32) of the 1,088 on the chip; every measurement here uses them at 600 MHz.
chip-minions.note: The other 64 are the master and spare shires (34 minion shires in all).

chip.advertised-range.statement: Advertised operating range: 300-800 MHz and about 40 W for the open-sourced platform (AI Foundry); Esperanto's papers give 300 MHz to 2 GHz.
chip.advertised-range.note: These cards' firmware only offers 600, 700 and 800 MHz (see clock.minion-opps).

chip.cm-shire-mask.statement: The driver reports compute shire mask 0xffffffff (shires 0-31) and sync (master) shire 32 on every card.
chip.cm-shire-mask.page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

chip.compute-array.statement: Typically 32 minion shires form the compute array and one more is the management (master) shire; the datasheet calls this a software convention, all minion shires being identical. The 34th is a yield-recovery spare, powered down in production.
chip.compute-array.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3: 'the 34th shire will be designated as a powered down yield recovery spare')

chip.cores-total.statement: The ET-SoC-1 has 1,093 RISC-V cores: 1,088 ET-Minions, 4 ET-Maxions and 1 Minion-based service processor.
chip.cores-total.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1 Product Overview); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.7 (§1)

chip.die-area.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:513; docs/findings/01-resources.md:234 (R14: Hot Chips 33 slide 20; IEEE Micro 42(3) p.37)

chip.die-dims.statement: Die about 25.6-25.8 mm east-west by 22.1-22.2 mm north-south (width/height 1.15-1.17), from the published die plot scaled to 570 mm²; the shire grid spans about 86% of the die's width, the rest being the memory shires and their DRAM PHYs down each side (about 1.76 mm per side).
chip.die-dims.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/geometry/pitch.json, `scale_from_570mm2.A_black_layout_region` and `.B_symmetric_bottom` (`die_w_mm`, `die_h_mm`, `grid_w_mm`, `memshire_col_w_mm`); heat-per-mm page §'How long is a hop'
chip.die-dims.note: Pixel measurement of a die plot; depends on what the 570 mm² covers. Use for proportions only.

chip.die-revision.statement: The datasheet's package marking example gives die revision A0; the driver reports arch_rev 0 on every card. Whether the lab cards are A0 has not been confirmed by AI Foundry.
chip.die-revision.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.34 (Table 10-1); docs/reports/data/2026-09-22-cards/driver_config.json `arch_rev`; docs/et-soc1-notes.md:342

chip.harts.statement: Software sees 2,048 harts on the 32 compute shires: hartid = shire × 64 + minion × 2 + thread (shire = hartid >> 6, neighbourhood = (hartid mod 64) >> 4, minion = hartid >> 1, thread = hartid & 1).

chip.hop-pitch.statement: Shire tile pitch 3.73 mm east-west and 3.70 mm north-south, so one mesh hop is about 3.72 mm (3.64-3.74 over three readings).
chip.hop-pitch.note: Kind A (estimate from the die plot) in the claims index.

chip.io-shire.statement: The I/O shire holds the Maxion neighbourhood (4 Maxions) with a shared L2/L3 cache, the service processor with ROM and 1 MB SRAM, a hardware root of trust, five PVT controllers and the peripherals (USB, I2C, SPI, UART, eMMC).
chip.io-shire.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.6, PVT controllers in the I/O shire)
chip.io-shire.note: Sources disagree on the Maxions' cache: the datasheet (pdf p.5) and PRM (pdf p.486) say 4 MB; the Shire Cache Specification (pdf p.22) says 'the IOShire has a cache total of 1 MB'.

chip.master-shire-id.statement: The master shire (which runs the master-minion firmware and schedules kernels) is shire 32 in the firmware; its 2.5 MB scratchpad at 0x9000_0000 holds the firmware's host-interface buffers.
chip.master-shire-id.note: layout.h:45 also reserves MASTER_SHIRE_COMPUTE_HARTS 32; minion_configuration.h:53 MM_MASTER_SHIRE_NEIGH_NUM 2.

chip.maxions.statement: Four ET-Maxion 64-bit RISC-V single-threaded superscalar out-of-order cores sit in the I/O shire with a system bus and coherency hub; they may be used for management tasks.
chip.maxions.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1) and pdf p.18 (§2.5.2)

chip.memshires.statement: Eight memory shires, four on the east side and four on the west side of the die, each driving two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels: 16 channels in all.
chip.memshires.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30 (§7); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.5)

chip.minion-shires.statement: 34 minion shires of 32 minions each = 1,088 minions. The hierarchy figure describes '34 Shires / 1,088 Minion cores and 4 Maxion cores in a 6 x 6 array'; with the PCIe and I/O shires (the Maxions sit in the I/O shire) that fills the 36 cells.
chip.minion-shires.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and Figure 2-1 on pdf p.6; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.8-9 (§1.2, Figure 1-1)

chip.minions.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.15 (§2.2.1)

chip.pcie-shire.statement: The PCIe shire contains two independent dual-mode PCIe controllers and an 8-lane PCIe Gen4 PHY, factory-configured as an endpoint; the dev card exposes a Gen4 x8 host interface.
chip.pcie-shire.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and pdf p.17 (§2.3, Figure 2-7)

chip.process.statement: TSMC 7 nm, over 24 billion transistors, 89 mask layers (Esperanto, Hot Chips 33 and IEEE Micro 2022).
chip.process.note: External, published by the vendor; not checked on these cards.

chip.service-processor.statement: The service processor is a single ET-Minion core (one hart, no vector or tensor extension, no shire cache) in the I/O shire, with its own ROM and 1 MB scratchpad SRAM; it boots the chip, runs the power/clock governor and answers the host's management commands.
chip.service-processor.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and pdf p.18 (§2.4); external/et-man/ET Introduction.pdf, pdf p.7 ('Service Processor is a minion without vector/tensor extensions')
chip.service-processor.page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

chip.spare-shire-id.statement: The spare shire is bit 33 of the firmware's 34-shire mask; the NoC reconfiguration code remaps virtual shire IDs when the spare displaces a shire.

chip.sram-total.statement: 140 MB of on-die SRAM (35 shire caches × 4 MB, counting the I/O shire's), each 1 MB block configurable as local L2, a slice of the chip-wide L3, or globally addressable scratchpad.
chip.sram-total.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3)
chip.sram-total.note: The I/O shire's cache is 1 MB in the Shire Cache Specification (pdf p.22), which would make it 137 MB.

clock.minion-opps.statement: Operating points the firmware uses: 600 MHz at 517 mV, 700 MHz at 568 mV, 800 MHz at 618 mV (measured on die); every table in the reports is at 600 MHz, where a warm card sits.
clock.minion-opps.page: The DVFS loop and its leakage
clock.minion-opps.cards_txt: aifoundry2 (aifoundry3 is pinned at 600 MHz, not measured here)

die.handedness.statement: The die view follows the firmware's NoC-spec drawing and the Programmer's Reference Manual's Fig. 1-3: memory shires 0-3 on the west, PCIe then I/O at the east end of the top row. The published die plot draws I/O then PCIe, its mirror image; no document in the open drop says which handedness the silicon has.
die.handedness.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-27-chip-diagram/research/firmware_map.json; fact L24 (PRM Fig. 1-3 against the die plot)

dram.capacity.statement: 32 GB of LPDDR4X on these V3 cards (Micron part): 2 GB per channel; the chip supports 8 to 32 GB.
dram.capacity.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.1; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:289; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.342 and p.552; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30

dram.channels.statement: 16 LPDDR4X channels of 16 bits (256 bits in all): each memory shire drives two channels, and four LPDDR4X packages of four channels (64 bits each) sit on the card.
dram.channels.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.5); external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.3; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4
dram.channels.note: The datasheet (pdf p.30) says two 16-bit PHYs share one 32-bit controller per memory shire; the firmware programs two uMCTL2 controller instances per memory shire (docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:286-287).

dram.controller-policy.statement: Controller configuration as programmed: open page, no auto-precharge, no power-down or self-refresh, no automatic ZQ, ECC off; tRCD = tRP = 18.2 ns, read latency 19.3 ns. DDR controller registers are service-processor only.

dram.counters.statement: Each memory shire has a perf monitor with a 40-bit cycle counter (933 MHz) and two event counters; the firmware sets them to count mesh reads and writes, which U-mode can sample through syscall 10.

dram.leg.statement: Past the L3, the DRAM leg costs 91 + 12 × hops(home shire, memory shire) cycles; about 25 of the 91 are the DRAM chip (activate 11, read and burst 14) and about 66 the memory shire. Only 25-28 of a ~300-cycle DRAM load are the DRAM's own timing.
dram.leg.source: docs/et-soc1-notes.md:166; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json `decomp.ms_const`; cards.json `ms_const` (90-91 on three cards); docs/findings/05-claims.md:404

dram.memshire-select.statement: The memory shire serving a line is PA[8:6] (so it is always the L3 home shire's low three bits) and the controller/channel within it is PA[9]: consecutive 64 B lines rotate over the 8 memory shires, the two channels alternate every 512 B.
dram.memshire-select.source: external/et-platform/device-minion-runtime/tools/zebumem.c:67-72, 120-121; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.26-27 (§1.4.3: 'the Memory Shire is selected by the NoC using bits [8:6]'); confirmed by the memory shires' read counters (syscall 10), docs/et-soc1-notes.md:166

dram.peak-card.statement: At 3,733 MT/s the 16 channels carry 119 GB/s.

dram.pkg-pairing.statement: Which two memory shires share each LPDDR4X device is not documented: the datasheet says only that two memory shires communicate with each 64-bit device. The diagram pairs neighbouring memory shires on each side (0 and 1, 2 and 3, 4 and 5, 6 and 7), after the block diagram's two LPDDR4X blocks per side, on the inferred die placement.
dram.pkg-pairing.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30 (§7: 'Two Memshires communicate with each 64-bit LPDDR4X memory device') and p.15 (Figure 2-6, fact L23)

dram.placeholder.statement: The 128,000 MB/s DRAM bandwidth the runtime reports is a placeholder constant in the service-processor firmware, not a measurement.

dram.rate-card.statement: The firmware hard-codes the 933 MHz DDR configuration on every card (controller clock 933 MHz, DRAM clock 1,866 MHz, 3,733 MT/s); telemetry reads mhz.ddr = 933 in every sample.

dram.rate-datasheet.statement: Datasheet rate: 4,266 MT/s, printed as 133 GB/s; 16 × 2 B × 4.266 GT/s is 136.5 GB/s (Esperanto's papers say 137).
dram.rate-datasheet.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1); docs/et-soc1-notes.md:20; docs/findings/05-claims.md:514

dram.row-bits.statement: Inside a channel: bank PA[12:10], column PA[17:13] (plus PA[5:1] within the line), row PA[18] and up (PA[34:18]); 8 banks, 2 KB page, one rank per channel.
dram.row-bits.note: Row/bank bits measured with one address bit flipped; the controller's ADDRMAP decode is the research agent's inference.

dram.unmetered.statement: About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail (DDR PHY, I/O rail and the DRAM chips); no meter covers the memory shires or DRAM.

e-add.statement: Integer add: 6.2 pJ [5.6-6.9] on zeros, 9.7 [9.3-10.3] on random operands, both harts of 1,024 minions flat out (little more than a nop, 5.1 pJ).

e-awake.statement: An awake minion (addi loop) costs about 2 mW (1.87 mW one hart, 3.02 mW both harts, aifoundry2); 5.1 / 6.6 pJ per instruction pooled over three cards.
e-awake.note: Keeping 1,024 minions awake for a second is 2-3.1 J, against 36 J for the card at 80 C.

e-dram.statement: DRAM: 114.6 pJ/B [89.0-141.3] above idle, 1 KB tensor loads (L1: 32 B vector loads) by every minion at 600 MHz; per card a2 111.5, a3 105.6, a1c1 126.6.
e-dram.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json: reruns.levels_pj_per_byte["dram"] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table 4.2
e-dram.note: About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail (DDR PHY, I/O, the DRAM chips); the E30 fit puts ~73 pJ/B of it off-rail.

e-dram-tload.statement: Tensor load from DRAM (catalogue, both data sets): 94.6 pJ/B [86.2-105.7] on zeros, 132.6 [117.9-145.4] on random data; tensor store to DRAM 94.4 / 141.9. Even DRAM is data-dependent.
e-dram-tload.note: Per card, random: a2 134.8, a3 127.3, a1c1 135.8 pJ/B.

e-dram-vs-scp.statement: DRAM is 30x the energy of the shire's own scratchpad per byte read, and 17x per byte written.
e-dram-vs-scp.note: Ratio of the catalogue rows above (random data).

e-dram-writeback.statement: Stores to DRAM through the L1 write-back path (fsw.ps): 341.5 pJ/B [317.4-373.3] on random data, 2.4x a tensor store, at 27 GB/s: each store allocates its line, so the byte pays a read and a write.

e-fadd.statement: Scalar float add fadd.s: 23.7 pJ [22.0-24.5] on zeros, 26.3 [24.1-27.0] on random data: 3.8x an integer add even on zeros (the FPU does not gate on zero).

e-fadd-ps.statement: 8-lane vector add fadd.ps: 22.4 pJ on zeros (same as the scalar op: lanes on zeros add nothing), 41.1 on random data (5.1 per lane).

e-fexp-ps.statement: Transcendental fexp.ps (8 lanes): 155.4 pJ [147.3-162.4] on random data at a quarter the issue rate; flog.ps 218 pJ. No hardware divide or square root: they trap.

fw.grey-cells.statement: In the firmware's maps the four cells that hold no compute shire are: logical (0, 3), shire 32, the master; (5, 3), shire 33, the spare; (0, 4), the PCIe shire ('pcie0' in the bridge map); and (0, 5), the I/O shire ('io0'). On this die view that puts the master in the north cell and the spare in the south one, with PCIe then I/O east of the master.
fw.grey-cells.note: To confirm on the cards: time a counter read on shire 32 from each compute shire (the hub's rung exp-mesh-stops).

fw.map-match.statement: Renamed as the boot firmware renames the shires (NOC_Remap_Shires with its 'No displacement' table, used when no shire is fused off), the firmware's 'default Shire Virtual ID Map, based on the NOC spec' matches the measured map: 496 of 496 pair distances and 32 of 32 cells, with no rotation or mirror. As written, before the renaming, only 111 of 496 pair distances agree (fact L37).

fw.memshires.statement: The firmware's map puts memory shires mc0-mc3 at logical rows 1-4 on the west (y = -1) and mc4-mc7 at rows 1-4 on the east (y = 6): the DRAM-latency fit's places for the 7 memory shires the fit places on its own, provided the firmware's mcN is the memory shire that PA[8:6] = N selects. With those 7 in place, memory shire 2 has one cell left in the firmware's map as in the fit (fact ms2-forced): the map confirms the frame, not memory shire 2's place independently.
fw.memshires.note: Timing a counter read on each memory shire from every compute shire (the hub's rung exp-mesh-stops) would place memory shire 2 directly.

hot-cost.statement: One contended global atomic (amoaddg.w on one line, 1,024 minions): the bank retires one every 10.00 cycles, about 60 M/s for the whole chip; spread over 32 lines, one per shire, 0.31 cycles and 1,919 M/s: 32x.
hot-cost.note: The atomic itself is fair: every shire gets 0.998-1.004 of an even split, the host included.
hot-cost.page: One hot line stops a shire

hot-edge.statement: The switch is sharp: 21 remote requesters leave the host at 95.5-95.7% of its rate, 22 stop it (0.02%). Rule: the bank is not saturated while N x 10 cycles < P + t_round_trip (216 cycles).
hot-edge.page: One hot line stops a shire

hot-energy.statement: Energy per atomic: 19.8 nJ [16.9-23.6] contended against 1.16 nJ [1.01-1.37] spread over 32 lines: 17x.

hot.cliff.statement: The host shire's minions read their own scratchpad while the same number of minions in one other shire hammer one scratchpad word in the host shire: with 21 of each the host keeps 95.6 / 95.7 / 95.6% of its rate alone (aifoundry2 / aifoundry3 / aifoundry1-c1, mean of 3 passes; 95.5-95.7% over every pass), and with 22, 23 or 24 it stops: 0.02% on every card. An uncontended remote atomic takes 216.2 / 216.3 / 216.6 cycles round trip.
hot.cliff.unit: % of the rate alone (21 requesters, aifoundry2)
hot.cliff.page: One hot line stops a shire

hot.fair.statement: All 32 shires hammering one global atomic homed in shire 0 (32 minions each): every shire gets an even share, the host shire 1.004 / 1.004 / 1.004 of it (1.004) and the lowest 0.998 / 0.998 / 0.999 (0.998-0.999; aifoundry2 / aifoundry3 / aifoundry1-c1), at 10.00 cycles per atomic.
